messages:
Zoe Kim: heads-up: deployed the quickstart that imports our SDK into Cloudflare Workers and got `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'` at startup. Works in Node locally. Any idea?
Evan Li: that usually means a CJS/ESM mismatch — either the bundle is shipping `export` syntax where the runtime expects CJS, or the sample is using `require()` on an ESM build. Which SDK version are you using?
Zoe Kim: pinned to `@redwood-inference/sdk@1.12.0`. Our sample did `const SDK = require('@redwood-inference/sdk')` in a helper. I assumed bundler would normalize it.
Grace Park: Cloudflare Workers + Wrangler runs native ESM. If your published package main is CJS (or `require` entry), but your bundler didn't transpile correctly, you'll see exports/require issues. Conversely if package is ESM and you `require()` it that's also bad.
Samir Desai: quick checklist: 1) check package.json `type` field and `exports` map; 2) ensure `dist/edge.mjs` is pure ESM and small; 3) provide a `dist/node.cjs` for CJS consumers. 4) publish types as `.d.ts` and point `types` to them.
Evan Li: also look for `module.exports =` leaking into code or `require('...').default` mismatch. With esbuild/rollup, use `format: 'esm'` for the edge build and `format: 'cjs'` for node build. Use `package.json` export conditions like:
`"exports": {"import": "./dist/edge.mjs","require": "./dist/node.cjs"}`
This helps consumers pick the right file.
Zoe Kim: our sample uses vite to bundle for Workers. Vite SSR step turned on CJS transform and produced a small shim that still referenced `exports` — that crashed.
Grace Park: Vite has SSR/build config gotchas. For Workers target use `build.target: 'es2020'` and `ssr: false` for the sample, or bypass Vite and use esbuild to emit an ESM module. Also set `esbuild.platform = 'browser'` to avoid injecting Node polyfills.
Samir Desai: types tip: TS consumers on Edge need DOM libs. But also if you ship ESM-only `.mjs` you should still ship `index.d.ts` that declares `export =` or `export default` consistently. Mismatch there causes `TS7016` or runtime `undefined` default exports.
Oliver Hall: minor runtime detection: don't attempt to feature-detect by `typeof process === 'undefined'` alone — some serverless envs fake process. Prefer `typeof globalThis?.fetch === 'function' && typeof process === 'undefined'` as a hint, but better is explicit builds.
Evan Li: for immediate workaround in the sample: change `require('@redwood-inference/sdk')` to `import sdk from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` and ensure Vite outputs ESM. That should stop the `export` token error.
Zoe Kim: switching to `import` fixed the syntax error in Wrangler dev. But now tests in Node that use `require()` broke. So we do need both builds.
Grace Park: exactly. For the SDK package we should: publish dual bundles, add `exports` map as Evan suggested, and add a tiny README section "Node vs Edge import guidance" with code snippets for `require` and `import` usage.
Samir Desai: CI suggestion: add a matrix job that installs the published tarball and runs a tiny Node script with `require()` and a Miniflare/Wrangler run that `import`s the edge entry. Catchs regressions early.
Devex-Bot: Internal note created: https://redwood-internal.example.com/devex/edge/esm-cjs-guidance Added recommended `exports` example, publish checklist, and CI test idea. :white_check_mark:
Zoe Kim: thanks y'all. I'll open a tiny PR to change the sample to `import` and file a follow-up issue for publishing dual bundles and adding the `exports` map. Will paste links when ready. :rocket:
